The BASIC programming language was origi.why: Rarely stated. Every exact form of the direct fact tried is absent from Dolma. The BASIC article states where it was created by college ("at Dartmouth College"), and names New Hampshire only through the 2019 historical marker in Hanover and a citation's place of publication; the Dartmouth BASIC article does not name the state. It follows from BASIC being developed at Dartmouth and Dartmouth being in Hanover, New Hampshire. Not very_likely: BASIC co-occurs with "Hanover, New Hampshire" a few hundred times, though mostly through Dartmouth's address. The verifier's extra searches (address forms such as 'BASIC was developed at Dartmouth College in Hanover', 'in New Hampshire': 0) found the direct fact only in the 2019 marker coverage ('birthplace of BASIC', 16 hits), so the rating stays likely.

notes: New derived record, replacing the scouting's Java (California to New York) and its PostScript backup. Both rest on 'a product is developed in its developer's headquarters state', which is a default, not a definition: Sun and Adobe had offices elsewhere, so a third world (developed by the company at an out-of-state office) keeps the company's headquarters and breaks the determinacy of the premise-route query ('In which state was the company that developed X headquartered?'). BASIC was built at one college campus, so the combining rule is location transitivity and holds in every world. Derivability likely, not very_likely: the BASIC article names New Hampshire once (the 2019 historical marker in Hanover), and BASIC co-occurs with 'Hanover, New Hampshire' a few hundred times, though no exact statement of the fact was found. Vermont is plausible (Dartmouth sits on the Connecticut River across from Norwich, Vermont) and clearly false. Every prompt says 'the BASIC programming language', since BASIC alone is also an ordinary word. 'Dartmouth College' is named in full because the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth is in Massachusetts. Since 2026-10-31 the worlds name only the premise that gives way and its side facts (another college, another town for Dartmouth), not Vermont, which each world now derives from the edit; and the one-state presupposition that q0, q2 (w1) and q3 (w2) rely on (and q1's 'no' before the edit) is stated as the bridge 'The BASIC programming language was originally developed in only one US state.' with a check (formal check, FINDINGS open decision 4).
